avatarPicker.dialog.description: How {name} appears in chats, contacts and desktops. An emoji and a colour make a team easy to tell apart at a glance.
avatarPicker.dialog.title: Avatar for {name}
botActivity.empty: This fills in as {name} works: every run posts here when it starts, waits or finishes.
botActivity.feed.delegatorDecides: The delegator decides whether to continue
botActivity.feed.stopped: A run was stopped by its delegator
botActivity.label: Activity
botActivity.schedule.body: Each entry wakes {name} at its time with the prompt as the task, in the background. Every firing shows up here as a run woken by a schedule.
botActivity.schedule.title: On a schedule
botProfile.experience.body: What {name} has learned from its own work: how a site behaves, which approach worked, what to avoid. After a task ends, the notes it took are consolidated into these entries in the background, and every future run reads them before it starts. Each entry names where it came from; one learned after reading untrusted content is held until you confirm it. Facts about the shared computer live on the Computer page, and your own instructions on the next tab.
botProfile.experience.title: Experience
botProfile.glance.title: At a glance
botSchedules.empty: No schedules yet. Add one, for example weekdays at 09:00.
botSchedules.intro: Wake {name} at set times with a task, without anyone writing a message. Each firing is a normal run and shows on the Activity tab. Times are cron (minute hour day month weekday) in {timeZone}; a firing that overlaps a running one is skipped.
botSchedules.nextUnavailable: Next occurrence unavailable for this draft.
botSchedules.title: Schedules
contacts.dialog.description: A new teammate in {workspace}, on its shared computer. Give it a handle people will @mention and a one-line role; you write its instructions on its profile afterwards.
contacts.dialog.draftRoleHelp: A model drafts its instructions for you to review. The bot starts after you apply or skip the draft.

management.bot.needWorkspace: Create a workspace before adding a bot.
management.bot.roleHelp: Role is a display description. After creation, write SOUL.md to give this bot executable instructions.
management.bots.title: Bots
management.egress.confirmRemoval: Remove {domains}? Existing connections to removed domains will be closed.
management.egress.title: Workspace egress
management.model.cheapIntro: A second, cheaper model handed to each run for side work such as summaries and memory consolidation. It is not a router: the task itself always runs on the model above, and nothing moves a request between models by price. Leave it on the deployment default unless you have a reason.
management.model.intro: Which model {name} thinks with. The deployment default follows the Gateway setting, so one change there moves every bot that did not pick its own.
management.model.label: Model
management.model.title: Model
management.openInternet.label: Open internet
management.openInternet.title: Allowlist is * : any public hostname. Private addresses and IP literals stay blocked. Keep production credentials out of this workspace.
management.restoration.body: An NSS database in temporary container storage was detected. Its contents and prior authorization are unverified. Before restoring from an audited workspace backup, check the original authorization, exact current peer fingerprints and expiry. Changed peers or expired grants need new authorization. Do not copy arbitrary root state or bypass certificate checks.
management.restoration.replacement_outco: Replacement outcome unknown; inspect the exact workspace
management.restoration.title: Temporary access restoration
management.rules.byHandIntro: A rule matches a tool, and optionally the site, a text the arguments must contain, or a file path. Only the tool is required; the fewer fields, the wider the rule.
management.rules.empty: No rules yet: every outside action still asks.
management.rules.intro: When {name} is about to do something with an outside effect, such as clicking Export, submitting a form or sending a message, it stops and asks in the chat. A rule answers in advance so the same action does not ask again. The easiest way to make one is the Always button on a request; here you can read, remove, or write one by hand.
management.rules.roleNote: write or remove an approval rule
management.rules.title: Approval rules
management.screen.title: Manage workspaces and bots
management.soul.changed: SOUL.md changed since it was loaded. Your draft is preserved.
management.soul.intro: Who {name} is and how it works, in plain Markdown (its SOUL.md). This is the one text that changes its behaviour; the role on the profile is only a label. Saving takes effect on the next run.
management.soul.keepDraft: Keep draft and use latest as base
management.soul.saved: SOUL.md saved. The next run starts a fresh session with this version.
management.soul.title: Instructions
management.soulDraft.applied: Applied. The next run starts a fresh session with these instructions.
management.soulDraft.failed: No draft: {error}. The saved instructions are unchanged.
management.soulDraft.instructionPlacehol: e.g. also review release notes, be more concise
management.soulDraft.intro: Describe the change in one sentence or a few keywords. A model drafts it; nothing is saved until you apply it.
management.soulDraft.noPermissions: Instructions describe behaviour only. They never grant tools, approvals, network access or authority.
management.soulDraft.pending: Drafting… This runs as a recorded model job and is billed to this workspace.
management.soulDraft.previewIntro: Proposed change against the loaded version. Lines marked + are added and - removed; everything else stays as it is.
management.soulDraft.saveFirst: Save or discard your own edits first.
management.soulDraft.stale: The instructions changed since this draft was made. Discard it and draft again against the current version.
management.soulDraft.title: Draft with AI
management.trash.intro: Archived workspaces and bots stay here until an Owner or Admin restores or permanently deletes them.
management.trash.title: Trash
management.tryIt.intro: Opens a private chat named "Test {name}". It is a normal run: same limits, same ledger, same costs.
management.tryIt.title: Try it
management.vision.label: Image input on {model}:
management.vision.reason.blocked: no bot in this workspace can run the test
management.vision.reason.explicit_refusa: the model said it cannot see images
management.vision.reason.no_transport_ev: no image was seen on the way to the model
management.vision.reason.not_probed: not tested for this configuration yet
management.vision.reason.wrong_answer: the test answer was wrong, so the model may describe images it cannot see
management.vision.withheld: Runs on this model are not shown images: pictures and screenshots reach it as a short text notice instead.
